target_customer: Citizens, activists, organizations and crypto networks needing censorship resistant voting and governance
problem: Democratic voting and governance tools are centralized and corruptible, and activists in repressive countries lack safe ways to hold votes.
business_model: Nonprofit funded by grants and token sales, open source software

founders.name: Santiago Siri
previous_startups: Partido de la Red (Net Party), co-started in 2012, won about 1 percent of the vote in Buenos Aires in 2013
founders.background_notes: Fast Forward article (2016-07-26) says he helped start the party in 2012 and later became an entrepreneur.

founders.name: Pia Mancini
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page and Fast Forward article.

founders.name: Guido Vilariño
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page; described elsewhere as CTO of DemocracyOS.

technical_complexity.rationale: Secure identity, anonymous voting and blockchain governance in 2015 were unsolved problems for a tiny team.

defensibility.rationale: Open source by design, so the code is freely copyable; value depended on adoption and reputation.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent targeted this niche; the project stayed a small nonprofit.

market_need_then: Argentina's Net Party experiment and its DemocracyOS software (2012 to 2013) showed activist interest in digital participation, though paying demand was weak.

branding.domain_note: democracy.earth, a custom domain extension rather than .com.

identity.mascot_or_character: Predecessor party Partido de la Red used a Trojan horse symbol
identity.voice_and_tone: Mission driven, global ('power in your hands')

branding.brand_signature: The Social Smart Contract white paper and Sovereign project
branding.community_and_virality: TED Global talk (2014) and awards such as MIT Technology Review (2017) listed on the YC page; press in Fast Company and Wired about Siri.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong press and conference visibility for a tiny nonprofit, with a mission led brand, but no sourced traction in product use.

pivots.why: Fast Forward (2016-07) describes blockchain liquid democracy voting as its focus; reason not stated.

outcome_analysis: Democracy Earth stayed a small nonprofit, with grants from Fast Forward (2016) and the Templeton Foundation (2019) and a 2017 token based proposal for the Sovereign voting platform. Revenue was reported at about 70 thousand dollars for 2021 and its Open Collective page is archived, so activity appears to have wound down, but no dated shutdown is documented. Success is hard to rate because it was never a venture style company.
notes: Company website fetch returned only a title. Aggregators list 100K to 120K seed amounts (Dealroom, unverified). Sovereign token sale proceeds not found. Directory status is Active while Open Collective says archived and no longer active, undated. No dated competitor source was found (Follow My Vote and LiquidFeedback existed but only in undated profiles), so competitors are empty. The YC listing may be a mix of Democracy Earth and DemocracyOS details.
